title: GitKraken graph with Undo/Redo toolbar and agent WIP nodes

pins.note: Undo/Redo in the toolbar: reverts only the most recent supported action
WIP node per worktree, here an agent session 'Awaiting Approval'
Sidebar toggles List vs Agents view
Remotes grouped by person in the sidebar

insight: GitKraken now frames the graph as a control surface for parallel coding agents, each with its own WIP node; undo is single-step.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal WIP/agent nodes in the graph, but back them with a multi-step op-log undo instead of last-action-only.

title: Fork main window: tabs, folder-grouped branches, graph, commit detail

pins.note: Branches grouped by folder prefix (aozgaa/, dev/, lego/)
Quick Launch: command palette for checkout, file history, custom commands
Compact graph lanes beside one-line commits
Commit / Changes / File Tree tabs for the selected commit

insight: Dense native UI, one repo per tab, palette-driven; the reference 'fast and friendly' classic client at $59.99 one-time.
gitgud: Claude's pick: match Fork's density and Quick Launch, add what it lacks: Linux, custom shortcuts and uncommitted changes in the graph.

title: Sublime Merge: hunk/line staging inside the commit summary

pins.note: Per-hunk Discard / Stage buttons inline with the diff
Selected lines become their own stageable chunk
Unstaged changes listed as the top row of the commit list
Find-as-you-type search across message, author, path, content

insight: Staging happens in the diff itself with no modal; speed comes from a custom toolkit and own git reader.
gitgud: Claude's pick: stage/discard controls on the hunk itself plus keyboard 'stage and next'; gix reads give us the same no-wait feel.

title: Tower 'Undo Anything': Ctrl+Z across commit, branch and stash actions

pins.note: Single shortcut: Ctrl+Z, redo with Shift+Ctrl+Z
Undo staging, discarding a chunk, deleting a file, the commit itself
Also undo merge, rebase and interactive rebase
Branch context menu actions are all reversible

insight: Tower makes undo a global keyboard habit covering working-copy, branch and stash operations, not a separate recovery tool.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal the Ctrl+Z contract wholesale, powered by a GitButler-style snapshot log so discards are recoverable too.

title: Tower drag-and-drop history rewriting with modifier keys

pins.note: Confirm dialog reminds the move can be undone via reflog
Drag commits in History to reorder (interactive rebase)
Drag commit to HEAD = cherry-pick; hold Alt = revert
Drop commit onto commit = squash; Alt = fixup

insight: Every history edit is a drag with an Alt variant; the confirm dialog explicitly tells users the escape hatch.
gitgud: Claude's pick: same drag verbs, but skip the confirm when the op log can undo it; confirm only what can't be undone (push).

title: GitHub Desktop: checkbox file list and click-to-select diff lines

pins.note: Checkbox per file = include in commit, no separate index view
Click gutter line numbers to include/exclude individual lines
Stashed changes drawer under the file list
Co-author picker in the commit box
Primary action button changes with state (Pull origin, 3 behind)

insight: Simplest model in the field: no visible index, no graph; the single state-aware sync button is its best idea.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal the state-aware primary sync button and gutter line selection; avoid hiding the graph (its #3 most-wanted issue).

title: SourceGit main window: sidebar, graph, commit information

pins.note: Worktrees and submodules are first-class sidebar sections
Graph lanes merged into the subject column
Toolbar: fetch, pull, push, stash, apply, branch, git-flow, bisect
Information / Changes / Files tabs for the selected commit
Signature verification badge next to the SHA

insight: A free MIT Avalonia clone of the Fork layout with LFS, worktrees, image diff and AI messages; maintainer capacity is its risk.
gitgud: Claude's pick: proof a free cross-platform client can cover Fork's feature set; differentiate on LFS locking, Unity merges and undo.

title: GitButler feature grid: stacked, parallel, unlimited undo, agents

pins.note: Stacked branches: dependent features reviewed and landed separately
Parallel branches: several branches applied in one folder
Unlimited undo/redo, even after commits
Move changes between commits, absorb, reorder
Agent-optimised CLI with structured output

insight: GitButler now sells itself as version control for agents; its mechanics (oplog, absorb, stacks) are the most advanced in the field.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal oplog undo, absorb and stacks on top of plain branches; don't adopt the workspace-merge model (no LFS).

title: GitButler operations history with per-entry Revert

pins.note: Hover an entry to get Revert
Tooltip: restores app and files to before this op; revert is undoable
Every operation type is logged, incl. discards
Revert 'Create commit' returns to just before that commit

insight: Snapshots of branch state, uncommitted work and conflicts are stored in the git object DB before each action, so restore is exact.
gitgud: Claude's pick: build gitgud's undo on the same snapshot-in-ODB idea; show it as a timeline panel plus Ctrl+Z.

title: GitButler parallel branches: but status vs git log of the workspace commit

pins.note: but status: each applied branch with short IDs for commits
Two branches live in the same working folder
Git sees a synthetic merge on gitbutler/workspace
Workspace commit merges both branches over main

insight: Virtual branches are a synthetic merge commit; other tools still work but see an unusual HEAD.
gitgud: Claude's pick: avoid as default for Unity repos; borrow the short-ID addressing for gitgud's agent CLI.

title: SmartGit Conflict Solver: three-way with one-click takes

pins.note: Ours | working tree | theirs, side by side
Connector bands link each conflict across panes
Toolbar take-left / take-right / both actions
One-click resolutions, external tool optional

insight: Classic three-pane solver where the middle pane is the editable working tree.
gitgud: Claude's pick: text conflicts need this baseline; gitgud's edge is a file-level step first for Unity assets.

title: Sourcetree (Max's baseline): graph, hunk reverse, binary before/after

pins.note: Graph + commit table with branch filter dropdowns
Per-hunk 'Reverse hunk' / stage buttons
Binary file shown as before/after image
Shelved and subrepositories in sidebar (Hg heritage)

insight: Feature-complete but maintenance-mode; Windows LFS slowness comes from per-file LFS calls and embedded git-lfs.
gitgud: Claude's pick: keep Sourcetree's familiar layout cues for Max, fix its LFS batching and add real undo.

title: lazygit TUI: numbered panels and command log

pins.note: Panels numbered 1-5: jump with a digit
Tabs inside a panel: Files / Worktrees / Submodules
Commits / Reflog tabs: undo walks the reflog
Command log shows the git commands just run

insight: Everything is one keystroke from a numbered panel; transparency comes from the always-visible command log.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal digit-jump panels and the command log; keep a mouse-first path too.

title: VS Code 3-way merge editor: Incoming, Current, Result

pins.note: Accept Incoming / Accept Combination per conflict
Mirror actions on the Current side
Editable Result pane below
Conflicts-remaining counter
Complete Merge stages the file

insight: Free IDE baseline Max already has: result pane plus a remaining-conflicts counter and a single finish action.
gitgud: Claude's pick: match the counter and Complete action; beat it with whole-file asset choices and Unity smart merge.

title: JetBrains Conflicts dialog: per-file Accept Yours/Theirs

pins.note: Resolve All Simple Conflicts in one click
Accept Yours / Accept Theirs for a whole file
All unresolved files listed up front
Resolve Manually opens the 3-pane editor

insight: Conflicts start as a file list with whole-file decisions; text merging is the second step, not the first.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal this as gitgud's conflict entry point; it fits prefabs, scenes and binary assets best.

title: GitComet (2026, Rust + GPUI + gix): graph with staging sidebar

pins.note: Uncommitted changes as the top graph row
Unstaged list always visible right of the graph
Staged area and commit box below
Worktrees section in the sidebar
Graph with merge nodes highlighted

insight: Newest serious OSS client, same gix read path as gitgud, and the only one advertising LFS locks plus git-annex.
gitgud: Claude's pick: benchmark against it on big repos; win on Unity awareness, undo and agent review.

title: GG: Tauri + Svelte GUI for jj with drag-rebase and Undo

pins.note: Context menu: new child, squash into parent, restore, abandon
Undo button backed by jj's operation log
Revset query box filters the log
Squash / Restore buttons on the working-copy commit
Push/fetch per remote from the status bar

insight: Built on gitgud's exact stack; treats history as always editable because every op is undoable.
gitgud: Claude's pick: steal the 'always mid-rebase, but safe' feel and study its Tauri/Svelte code as a reference.
